**Sam Altman** is the current CEO of OpenAI as of May 2026. Here is a detailed overview of who he is and his role at the company:

Sam Altman is CEO of OpenAI, the artificial intelligence company that developed ChatGPT. He was president of the start-up accelerator Y Combinator from 2014 to 2019 and became CEO of OpenAI in 2019.

Sam Altman and Elon Musk were co-chairs of OpenAI when it was founded in 2015. OpenAI was established as a nonprofit aiming to create advanced AI for the benefit of humanity, but by 2017, the founders were convinced they needed to set up a for-profit arm to raise money and attract researchers in order to be competitive. In 2018, Musk proposed taking control of the organization to compete more directly with other AI companies, including Google, but Altman declined. Musk then left OpenAI, and the split reflected broader differences over how AI should be developed, governed, and commercialized.

Altman remained CEO of OpenAI after the board's reconstitution, and the company continued to expand its artificial intelligence products and partnerships, including its work with Microsoft.

Most recently, Altman has been at the center of a major legal battle. In 2024, Musk sued OpenAI, Altman, Greg Brockman, and Microsoft, claiming that the company had abandoned its original nonprofit mission in favor of commercial interests. Musk also sought the dismissal of Altman and Brockman from their posts, as well as the dismantling of the for-profit entity. However, the jury dismissed all claims in Elon Musk's lawsuit against OpenAI CEO Sam Altman. Musk lost the lawsuit in May 2026, with the jury concluding that he waited beyond the three-year statute of limitations to sue OpenAI.

On the business side, also in May 2026, Bloomberg reported that OpenAI was preparing to confidentially file its initial public offering, seeking to publicly debut in the Fall of that same year.

In summary, Sam Altman continues to lead OpenAI as its CEO as of May 2026, having successfully defended his position in a high-profile legal battle and steering the company toward a potential IPO [1][2][3][4].
